subject: Architecture
title: The Statue of Liberty: Engineering a Symbol
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Statue of Liberty: Engineering a Symbol.

hook.text: The Statue of Liberty's skin is thinner than two pennies stacked together.

buildup.text: Frédéric Bartholdi sculpted the copper exterior. Gustave Eiffel engineered the iron skeleton inside.

discovery.text: The statue was shipped from France in 350 pieces packed in 214 crates, then assembled on site.

twist.text: America couldn't afford the pedestal. Joseph Pulitzer raised funds through small newspaper donations.

climax.text: Its green color is natural patina — the original copper was shiny brown like a new penny.

punchline.text: France built it. America almost couldn't afford to stand it up.

quiz.question: Who engineered the Statue of Liberty's internal structure?
